authority.name: Educational insert accompanying sale of hypodermic syringes and needles

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 27 provides that hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles for the administration of controlled substances by injection may be sold in the commonwealth only by a pharmacist or wholesale druggist licensed under the provisions of chapter 112, a manufacturer of or dealer in surgical supplies or a manufacturer of or dealer in embalming supplies. The section states no prescription, age, identification, quantity or record requirement. Sections 47 and 48 of chapter 208 of the Acts of 2018 struck from s. 27 the words ', but only to persons who have attained the age of 18 years and' and struck its second sentence, which as enacted by chapter 172 of the Acts of 2006 had provided that when selling hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles without a prescription, a pharmacist or wholesale druggist must require proof of identification that validates the individual's age; section 49 of the same act struck from s. 32I the words 'to persons over the age of 18'. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 32I(a) no person shall sell, possess or purchase with intent to sell, or manufacture with intent to sell drug paraphernalia knowing, or under circumstances where one reasonably should know, that it will be used for purposes that include introducing a controlled substance into the human body in violation of chapter 94C, and under s. 32I(d) the section shall not apply to the sale of hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles pursuant to s. 27. Under M.G.L. c. 111, s. 25K the department shall develop an educational insert to accompany the sale of hypodermic syringes and needles, including but not limited to information on the proper use of hypodermic syringes and needles, the risk of blood-borne diseases that may result from their use and methods for preventing contracting or transmitting such diseases, proper hypodermic syringe and needle disposal practices, and the toll-free telephone numbers of the commonwealth's AIDS and Hepatitis C hotlines and the Massachusetts Substance Abuse Information and Education Helpline, and the educational insert shall be provided to purchasers of hypodermic syringes or needles at the point of sale.
exceptions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 32I does not apply to the sale of hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles pursuant to s. 27.

authority.name: Self-certification fee; time and method of fee payment
Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.35 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(vii)-(viii), each regulated seller must ensure that, for individuals who are responsible for delivering scheduled listed chemical products into the custody of purchasers or who deal directly with purchasers by obtaining payments for the products, the seller has submitted to the Administration a self-certification that all such individuals have, in accordance with criteria issued by the Administration, undergone training provided by the seller to ensure that they understand the requirements of part 1314, and that the seller maintains a copy of each self-certification and all records demonstrating that those individuals have undergone the training. Under 21 CFR 1314.40 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(B), a regulated seller must submit that self-certification in order to sell any scheduled listed chemical product; the certification is not effective unless it also includes a statement that the seller understands each of the requirements of the part and agrees to comply with them; when the seller files the initial self-certification the Administration assigns it to one of twelve groups, the self-certifications of a group expire on the last day of the month designated for that group, and the Administration may select a group with an expiration date that is not less than 12 months or more than 23 months from the date of the self-certification; after the initial certification period the seller must update the self-certification annually; and the seller must provide a separate certification for each place of business at which it sells scheduled listed chemical products at retail. Under 21 CFR 1314.42 the seller must pay a fee of $21 for each initial application to self-certify and for the renewal of each existing self-certification, at the time of self-certification, by credit card, and the fee is not refundable, but the fee is waived for any person holding a current DEA registration in good standing as a pharmacy to dispense controlled substances. Under 21 CFR 1314.50 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(G), a regulated seller may take reasonable measures to guard against employing individuals who may present a risk with respect to the theft and diversion of scheduled listed chemical products, which may include, notwithstanding State law, asking applicants for employment whether they have been convicted of any crime involving or related to such products or controlled substances.
exceptions: 21 CFR 1314.42(b) waives the self-certification fee for any person holding a current DEA registration in good standing as a pharmacy to dispense controlled substances; it waives only the fee.

authority.name: 247 CMR: Board of Registration in Pharmacy

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: As of 2026-09-16, none of the Massachusetts statutes and regulations searched adds a requirement for the retail sale of scheduled listed chemical products, the products containing ephedrine, pseudoephedrine or phenylpropanolamine that are regulated by 21 U.S.C. 830(d)-(e), 21 U.S.C. 844(a) and 21 CFR part 1314: no section of M.G.L. c. 94C, no chapter of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's regulations at 247 CMR 2.00 through 21.00, and no section of the Department of Public Health's regulation at 105 CMR 700.000 addresses these products or adds a requirement to those federal requirements.

authority.name: Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.30(a) and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), except for a purchase by an individual of a single sales package containing not more than 60 milligrams of pseudoephedrine, the regulated seller must maintain a written or electronic list of each scheduled listed chemical product sale that identifies the products by name, the quantity sold, the names and addresses of the purchasers, and the dates and times of the sales (the logbook). 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iv) applies the identification and logbook-signature requirements in the case of a sale to which that logbook requirement applies. Under 21 CFR 1314.30(b) the regulated seller must not sell a scheduled listed chemical product at retail unless the purchaser presents an identification card that provides a photograph and is issued by a State or the Federal Government, or a document that, with respect to identification, is considered acceptable for purposes of 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v)(A) and 274a.2(b)(1)(v)(B); the purchaser signs the logbook, for a written logbook by entering his name, address, and the date and time of the sale, and for an electronic logbook by signing a device presented by the seller that captures signatures electronically and displays the warning notice, a bound paper book carrying a printed sticker or a unique identifier linked to the sale information, or a printed document produced by the seller at the time of sale that is inserted into a binder or other secure means of document storage immediately after the purchaser signs; and the seller enters in the logbook the name of the product and the quantity sold. Under 1314.30(c), if the purchaser enters the name, address, date and time, the seller must determine that the name entered corresponds to the name provided on the identification and that the date and time entered are correct, and if the seller enters the information, the prospective purchaser must verify that it is correct. Under 1314.30(d) the seller must include in the logbook, or display by it, a notice that under 18 U.S.C. 1001 whoever, with respect to the logbook, knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals, or covers up a material fact, makes a materially false statement or representation, or makes or uses a false writing or document shall be fined not more than $250,000 if an individual or $500,000 if an organization, imprisoned not more than five years, or both. Under 1314.30(e)-(h), the seller must maintain each logbook entry for not fewer than two years after the date on which the entry is made; records must be kept at the regulated seller's place of business where the transaction occurred, except that they may be kept at a single, central location of the seller if the seller has notified the Administration of the intention to do so by written notification submitted by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Divisional Office for the area in which the records are required to be kept; the records must be readily retrievable and available for inspection and copying by authorized employees of the Administration; and a record developed and maintained to comply with a State law may be used to meet the requirements of 1314.30 if it includes the information that section specifies. Under 21 CFR 1314.45 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(C) and (E), logbook information shall be disclosed as appropriate to the Administration and to State and local law enforcement agencies; it shall not be accessed, used, or shared for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with this title or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety; and a regulated seller who in good faith releases logbook information to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct.
exceptions: A purchase by an individual of a single sales package containing not more than 60 milligrams of pseudoephedrine is excepted from the logbook requirement, and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(iv) applies the identification and signature requirements only to sales to which the logbook requirement applies.

Records may be kept at a single, central location of the regulated seller instead of the place of business where the transaction occurred if the seller has given the Administration the required written notification.
A record developed and maintained to comply with a State law may be used to meet 21 CFR 1314.30 if it includes the information that section specifies.

authority.name: Requirements regarding packaging of nonliquid forms
Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.05 and 21 U.S.C. 830(d)(2), a regulated seller or mail order distributor may not sell a scheduled listed chemical product in nonliquid form (including gel caps) unless the product is packaged either in blister packs, with each blister containing no more than two dosage units or, if blister packs are technically infeasible, in unit dose packets or pouches. Under 21 CFR 1314.25 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(i), (ii) and (ix)(I), each regulated seller must ensure that sales of a scheduled listed chemical product at retail are made in accordance with 1314.25 and 1314.20; must place the product so that customers do not have direct access to the product before the sale is made (behind-the-counter placement), a placement that includes circumstances in which the product is stored in a locked cabinet that is located in an area of the facility where customers do have direct access; and must deliver the product directly into the custody of the purchaser. Mobile retail vendors must place the product in a locked cabinet.
exceptions: Where blister packs are technically infeasible, a nonliquid form may be packaged in unit dose packets or pouches.
Behind-the-counter placement includes storing the product in a locked cabinet located in an area of the facility where customers do have direct access.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.15, each regulated person must report to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Divisional Office for the area in which the regulated person making the report is located any unusual or excessive loss or disappearance of a scheduled listed chemical product under the control of the regulated person, and the regulated person responsible for reporting a loss in-transit is the supplier. Each report must, whenever possible, be made orally to the DEA Divisional Office for that area at the earliest practicable opportunity after the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances involved; written reports of losses must be filed within 15 days after the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances of the event; a report must include a description of the circumstances of the loss (in-transit, theft from premises, etc.); and the section provides a suggested format for the report.
DEA-required controlled-substance inventories and records must be maintained and available for inspection for at least two years unless another provision requires longer.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Necessity of prescription for dispensing controlled substances
Electronic prescription requirement and the commissioner's exceptions

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 17(a) no controlled substance in Schedule II may be dispensed without an electronic prescription from a practitioner, except that under s. 17(b), IN EMERGENCY SITUATIONS, AS DEFINED BY THE COMMISSIONER, a schedule II, III, IV, V or VI substance may be dispensed upon written prescription or oral prescription IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 20 AND RELATED REGULATIONS; under s. 17(c) a controlled substance included in Schedule III, IV, V or VI shall not be dispensed without an electronic prescription from a practitioner. Under s. 23(g) prescribers shall issue an electronic prescription for all controlled substances and medical devices, and the department shall promulgate regulations setting forth standards for electronic prescriptions. Under s. 23(h) THE COMMISSIONER, THROUGH REGULATION, SHALL ESTABLISH EXCEPTIONS to section 17 and subsection (g) authorizing the limited use of a written and oral prescription where appropriate, and the exceptions SHALL BE LIMITED TO: (i) prescriptions issued by veterinarians; (ii) prescriptions issued or dispensed in circumstances where electronic prescribing is not available due to temporary technological or electrical failure; (iii) a time-limited waiver process for practitioners who demonstrate economic hardship, technological limitations that are not reasonably within the control of the practitioner, or other exceptional circumstance; (iv) prescriptions that are issued or dispensed in emergency situations as defined by the commissioner pursuant to said section 17, including situations where the electronic prescription requirement would result in a delay that would adversely impact the patient's medical condition; (v) when a prescription cannot be issued electronically under federal or state law or regulations; (vi) prescriptions issued outside the jurisdiction of the commonwealth; and (vii) other exceptions to said section 17 and said subsection (g) as the commissioner determines necessary, provided that 90 days before promulgating or amending any regulations regarding other exceptions the commissioner files a written report setting forth the justification with the house and senate committees on ways and means, the joint committee on public health, and the joint committee on mental health, substance use and recovery.
exceptions: Section 17(b) permits written or oral dispensing of a schedule II through VI substance in emergency situations as defined by the commissioner, in accordance with section 20 and related regulations.
The s. 23(h) exceptions take effect as the commissioner establishes them through regulation rather than directly from the statute.

authority.name: Advisory: Sale of Hypodermic Syringes and Needles

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Advisory on the Sale of Hypodermic Syringes and Needles (adopted December 6, 2016; the PDF listed among the Board's pharmacy practice resources is marked revised 12/14/21) informs licensees that M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 27 authorizes pharmacies to sell hypodermic syringes and needles to any person, of any age, without a prescription, and without identification; that the legislation does not limit the number or type of syringes and needles that may be sold to any one customer; and that no requirements or limitations exist to prevent a customer from acquiring hypodermic syringes and needles. As recommended action it states that the pharmacy should complete the sale of requested hypodermic syringes and/or needles without any further requirements or record keeping; that there is no need to restrict the quantity or type (e.g., IM syringes) of hypodermic syringes or needles that may be sold; that it is strongly recommended that the pharmacy stock single unit-of-use syringes for individual sale; and that pharmacies may provide information regarding proper use and disposal of needles and syringes.

Persons registered to manufacture, distribute, dispense, or possess controlled substances shall keep records and maintain inventories in conformance with the record-keeping and inventory requirements of the federal Comprehensive Drug Prevention and Control Act of 1970 or any amendment thereof, and the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, and with any additional rules or regulations promulgated by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy in the case of a retail drug business or wholesale druggist, or by the Commissioner in all other cases.

authority.name: Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(C), in order to protect the privacy of individuals who purchase scheduled listed chemical products, the Attorney General shall by regulation establish restrictions on disclosure of information in logbooks under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), and the regulations shall provide for the disclosure of the information as appropriate to the Attorney General and to State and local law enforcement agencies and prohibit accessing, using, or sharing information in the logbooks for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with the subchapter or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety. 21 CFR 1314.45 restricts the disclosure of information in logbooks under 21 CFR 1314.30 as follows: (a) the information shall be disclosed as appropriate to the Administration and to State and local law enforcement agencies; (b) the information in the logbooks shall not be accessed, used, or shared for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with this title or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety; and (c) a regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct. 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(E) states the same immunity for a regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii). Under 21 U.S.C. 842(a)(14) it is unlawful for any person who is a regulated seller or an employee or agent of such seller to disclose, in violation of regulations under 830(e)(1)(C), information in logbooks under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), or to refuse to provide such a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities. Under 842(c)(1)(A), except as provided in 842(c)(1)(B), (C) or (D) and 842(c)(2), any person who violates section 842 is subject to a civil penalty; subparagraphs (B) through (D) address violations of 842(a)(5), (10), (16) and (17). Under 842(c)(2)(A), if a violation of section 842 is prosecuted by an information or indictment which alleges that the violation was committed knowingly and the trier of fact specifically finds that it was so committed, the person shall, except as otherwise provided in 842(c)(2)(B) or (D), be sentenced to imprisonment of not more than one year or a fine under title 18, or both, and under 842(c)(3), except under the conditions specified in 842(c)(2), a violation of section 842 does not constitute a crime. 21 CFR 1300.02 defines a regulated seller as a retail distributor (including a pharmacy or a mobile retail vendor), except that the term does not include an employee or agent of the distributor.
exceptions: A regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct.

authority.name: Authority and criteria for classification of substances
Schedules of Controlled Substances: excluded and exempted substances and preparations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 811(g)(1) the Attorney General shall by regulation exclude any non-narcotic drug which contains a controlled substance from the application of subchapters I and II of chapter 13 of title 21 if such drug may, under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, be lawfully sold over the counter without a prescription. Under 21 CFR 1308.21(a) a person seeking to have such a nonnarcotic drug excluded from any schedule under 811(g)(1) may apply to DEA, and 21 CFR 1308.22 lists the nonnarcotic substances which may lawfully be sold over the counter without a prescription and are excluded from all schedules under 811(g)(1). Under 811(g)(3) the Attorney General may, by regulation, exempt any compound, mixture, or preparation containing a controlled substance from the application of all or any part of subchapter I if he finds that it meets the requirements of one of the following categories: (A) a mixture, or preparation containing a nonnarcotic controlled substance, which mixture or preparation is approved for prescription use, and which contains one or more other active ingredients which are not listed in any schedule and which are included therein in such combinations, quantity, proportion, or concentration as to vitiate the potential for abuse; (B) a compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any controlled substance, which is not for administration to a human being or animal, and which is packaged in such form or concentration, or with adulterants or denaturants, so that as packaged it does not present any significant potential for abuse; and (C) upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health and Human Services, a compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any anabolic steroid, which is intended for administration to a human being or an animal, and which, because of its concentration, preparation, formulation or delivery system, does not present any significant potential for abuse. DEA's provisions on excluded and exempted substances and preparations are 21 CFR 1308.21 and 1308.22 (exclusion of nonnarcotic substances that may lawfully be sold over the counter without a prescription), 1308.23 and 1308.24 (exempt chemical preparations intended for laboratory, industrial, educational, or special research purposes and not for general administration to a human being or other animal), 1308.25 and 1308.26 (exclusion under 21 U.S.C. 802(41)(B)(i) of anabolic steroid products expressly intended for administration through implants to cattle or other nonhuman species), 1308.31 and 1308.32 (exemption under 811(g)(3)(A) of compounds, mixtures, or preparations containing a nonnarcotic controlled substance, listed as exempted prescription products), 1308.33 and 1308.34 (exemption of compounds, mixtures, or preparations containing an anabolic steroid, intended for administration to a human being or animal, that because of concentration, preparation, formulation, or delivery system have no significant potential for abuse) and 1308.35 (exemption of certain processed cannabis plant material and animal feed mixtures that are not used, or intended for use, for human consumption). Under 21 U.S.C. 802(17)(A) and (F) the term narcotic drug includes opium, opiates, derivatives of opium and opiates, and any compound, mixture, or preparation which contains any quantity of any of them.

Implementation of M.G.L. c. 94C

authority.name: Department of Public Health drug regulations
247 CMR: Board of Registration in Pharmacy

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 4 allows the commissioner acting jointly with the board of registration in pharmacy to except a compound, mixture or preparation from the application of all or any part of chapter 94C only by regulation pursuant to chapter 30A, only if its three conditions are met, the third being that the compound, mixture or preparation has been similarly excepted under the federal Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act of 1970 or any amendment thereof, and the regulation shall state the weight of the controlled substance. Under s. 5, controlled substances which are excepted pursuant to s. 4 may be dispensed, or sold at retail, subject to the conditions of that section. As of 2026-09-16, no regulation excepting any compound, mixture or preparation under s. 4 appears in the Massachusetts regulations searched: 105 CMR 700.000, Implementation of M.G.L. c. 94C (the edition published in Mass. Register #1514, 2/2/2024), in which 700.002(A) through (E) establish Schedules I through V as the drugs and other substances listed in 21 CFR 1308.11 through 1308.15 and 700.002(F) establishes Schedule VI as all prescription drugs not included in any other schedule, without stating any exception, and whose regulatory authority cites M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 2, 6, 24 and 24A but not s. 4; the Department of Public Health's other drug regulations listed in the mass.gov 105 CMR law library, 105 CMR 720.000, 721.000, 722.000, 724.000 and 726.000; and each chapter of the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's regulations listed in the mass.gov 247 CMR law library (247 CMR 2.00, 3.00, 4.00, 6.00, 7.00, 8.00, 9.00, 10.00, 11.00, 13.00, 14.00, 15.00, 16.00, 20.00 and 21.00). On those regulations there is at present no excepted preparation to which s. 5 applies.
